annotations.keyFindings: Across 11 studies with 2,480 patients, nurse-led titration increased the proportion at target dose (risk ratio 1.62) and reduced all-cause hospitalisation (risk ratio 0.78); the effect on mortality was imprecise.
annotations.limitations: Heterogeneous protocols; no included study titrated SGLT2 inhibitors; unblinded outcome assessment in most trials; search ended in 2021.

annotations.keyFindings: Patients valued continuity with one nurse; frequent blood tests were the main burden; several patients aged over 80 preferred clinic visits to telephone calls.
annotations.limitations: 22 patients from one clinic; interviews after titration was complete.

annotations.limitations: Consecutive series without comparison; primary care results not captured.

annotations.keyFindings: Consensus framework of 18 competences; recommends a signed-off written protocol, supervised practice for the first 20 patients and a six-monthly safety review.
annotations.limitations: Consensus without outcome data; predates SGLT2 inhibitors.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. A randomised comparison and a systematic review of 11 studies agree that nurse-led titration raises the proportion of patients reaching target doses and lowers hospitalisation; the pooled studies predate SGLT2 inhibitors. Two service reports from district settings describe four-class and post-discharge titration with potassium-related holds and dose reductions but few serious events, without comparison groups. Patients value continuity and dislike frequent blood tests, and missed visits are commoner in deprived areas, a gap that telephone visits narrowed. The effectiveness question is answered well enough to act on; local safety with four classes and equitable access are what remain to monitor.
gradeRationale: Randomised and pooled evidence with a consistent direction for doses reached and hospitalisation, downgraded for unblinded outcome assessment and for indirectness to four-class titration with SGLT2 inhibitors. Safety and access findings come from uncontrolled service data and are low certainty on their own.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; five source-derived claims recorded with passages; overall certainty moderate.
